description: Stable case catalog for the public-safe messy .NET workspace regression slice. Cases are marked implemented or deferred; this catalog is an inventory and does not claim deferred cases are proven. Implemented cases are pinned by src/dotnet/tests/TraceMap.Tests/MessyWorkspaceRegressionTests.cs.

artifactPinning.determinismContract: repeat CLI scans of each root produce byte-identical facts.ndjson
artifactPinning.generatorAndInputHashes: no new derived machine-readable artifact is introduced by this slice; provenance stays in the existing scan manifest (scanner version, commit SHA) and rule-catalog extractor versions
artifactPinning.failureIdentification: every test assertion names the catalog case id and the pipeline stage: extraction, combining, reconciliation, or traversal

cases.shape: handler chain of twelve call edges across Pages/, Services/, and Data/ folders ending in an ADO.NET-style supported SQL terminal at graph distance 14, beyond depths 8, 10, and 12
cases.assertions: at max depth 12 the terminal inventory is complete with identical boundary identity sets at depths 12 and 16 and minimum terminal distance 14; path enumeration honestly truncates with the depth reason while the terminal stays inventoried (no false absence); at depth 10 the distance-14 terminal falls outside the depth-bounded retained closure and the observation must scope its completeness claim to the retained graph instead of implying or inventing a terminal

cases.shape: three-node call cycle (First -> Second -> Third -> First) entered from a page handler
cases.assertions: traversal terminates on the cycle branch, records cycle truncation honestly, and reports the branch as downstream-without-supported-terminal rather than inventing a terminal

cases.shape: self-recursive method (Self calls Self) entered from its own dedicated page handler
cases.assertions: the self-cycle handler's own chain is selected independently of the three-node cycle: traversal terminates, records cycle truncation, inventories zero terminals, and surfaces its own scoped downstream-without-terminal gap

cases.shape: the same method names Process and Core in ten classes in one file, each ending in a distinct SQL terminal
cases.assertions: ten container-distinct identities survive extraction; traversal inventories ten distinct terminal witnesses; no call edge joins one engine's Process or Core to another engine's container

cases.shape: three independently scanned roots combined into one merged review with explicit labels
cases.assertions: combined sources, facts, and symbols are the union of the inputs with per-source namespacing and no symbol deduplication; root-beta reuses the Process/Core simple names from root-alpha and all eleven original Process identities stay distinct rows; every DatabaseOperationCandidate terminal stays attributed to its own source label (15 alpha, 1 beta, 1 vb) with its own table identity; the merged dependency report lists all three labeled sources; the Web Forms packet stays single-page-source by design, so cross-source attribution is asserted over the merged index directly

cases.shape: loose VB files with no .vbproj or .sln, including an App_Code folder, scanned through the portable Roslyn syntax fallback
cases.assertions: analysis level is Level3SyntaxAnalysis; the fail-closed workspace gap is present at Tier4; the data-adapter fill produces a Tier3 database operation attached to the handler; no blocker exists for projectless VB in ordinary CI

cases.shape: source spread across nested folders (Pages/, Services/, Data/, App_Code/) inside one root and across independently scanned roots
cases.assertions: call edges span folders with folder-relative file paths and the deep chain crosses the Services/ to Data/ boundary

cases.shape: one Web Forms handler invokes int and string interface overloads across two candidate implementations, each ending at its own SQL terminal
cases.assertions: the two semantic interface call targets and four implementation relationships retain their int/string signatures without cross-overload joins; the bounded Web Forms packet inventories four distinct candidate terminals

cases.shape: an interface-typed receiver with two possible concrete implementations per overload; runtime receiver selection is unknown
cases.assertions: four relationship-backed candidate edges join the exact semantic interface call identities; all four supported terminals remain distinct and every candidate boundary is NeedsReviewStaticPath rather than a proven runtime dispatch

cases.shape: one buildable three-project C# to VB to F# call chain, with F# compiled metadata admitted but F# source ownership unsupported
cases.assertions: the public projects build, the C# to VB hop is either semantic or explicitly downgraded to syntax plus a compilation gap, the VB to F# call is semantic, the F# compiled method is inventoried, and unsupported F# source ownership emits a gap rather than a guessed join; no complete cross-language source traversal is claimed

cases.shape: a Web Forms handler calls an auto-generated designer bridge that calls a hand-written SQL terminal
cases.assertions: the semantic handler call into the generated member is visible, but the excluded generated body is not invented as source call evidence; source traversal reports no terminal and an explicit terminal-evidence gap

cases.shape: the public generated-root handler's source method, exact admitted metadata method, operand-aware IL body, and portable PDB sequence point share one compiled fact identity
cases.assertions: a pinned public build and binding receipt yield one exact source-to-metadata handler edge; its compiled fact ID owns an IL body, one metadata-PDB method edge, and a sequence point; this does not claim rewritten PDB offset validity, ILAsm/ILDAsm parity, or runtime behavior

cases.shape: projectless VB Web Forms handler enters a dispatcher that calls five same-name Process methods in one file; two branches continue through unqualified or Me-qualified ContinueRoute calls to distinct SQL terminals
cases.assertions: five typed receiver calls and exact source-local bridges remain distinct; depth 8 and 10 inventory the same two supported terminal identities without crossing into sibling Process methods

cases.shape: a separate same-name Web Forms handler traverses Process, Forward, and Finish but has no supported SQL terminal
cases.assertions: depth 8 and 10 complete retained-graph terminal reachability with zero supported terminals and a selected-chain downstream-without-terminal gap; this never proves runtime absence

cases.shape: a third same-name handler traverses Process, Forward, and Execute to one supported SQL terminal
cases.assertions: depth 8 and 10 retain the same single terminal identity independently from the page-two and page-three routes

cases.shape: three projectless VB Web Forms pages and their backend classes are scanned as independent roots, then combined; page two branches through five same-name methods in one backend file to two SQL terminals, page three reaches none, and page eleven reaches one
cases.assertions: each page has exactly one cross-root receiver bridge; the merged packet retains complete 2/0/1 supported-terminal inventories and matching boundaries; this proves only the synthetic retained graph, not private-corpus behavior or runtime absence

cases.shape: a projectless VB Web Forms DropDownList Init Handles handler iterates New SyntheticDataAccess().MyList inside With; its explicit constructor calls an inline-created service, which forwards through a typed repository field and a typed SQL gateway field to an ADO.NET command terminal
cases.assertions: the control Init binding, two inline unassigned New expressions, exact creation-to-constructor edge, inline service call, two typed-field call hops, and one reachable SQL terminal remain visible after independent scans and combine; property value flow, collection contents, execution, and successful binding are not claimed

cases.shape: two independent backend roots contain the same unqualified VB type name and same-arity explicit constructor, while the page uses an inline New expression
cases.assertions: the duplicate constructor type identities produce an explicit Tier4 ambiguity gap and cannot create a terminal path from the page

cases.shape: a projectless VB dropdown Init handler creates an unqualified data-access type imported from one explicit namespace; its constructor calls two same-name helper methods before SQL, while an unrelated same-simple-name constructor in a second namespace has its own SQL decoy
cases.assertions: only the explicitly imported qualified constructor is bridged, the helper chain reaches one supported SQL terminal with complete retained-graph reachability, and source-local symbol reconciliation cannot merge the unrelated same-name constructor into a false second terminal

cases.shape: an unqualified projectless VB constructor creation has explicit Imports for two namespaces with same-name same-arity constructor declarations
cases.assertions: competing imported constructor identities fail closed with an explicit ambiguity gap and zero invented SQL terminals

cases.shape: two independent backend roots declare the same service type and method reached by an inline New service invocation in a projectless VB constructor
cases.assertions: the inline-created service type stays ambiguous across combined roots, emits a Tier4 receiver gap, and cannot create a terminal path from the page

cases.shape: projectless VB constructs a nested type after a generic outer type and calls through a parenthesized inline New receiver; a creation in its lexical namespace resolves only that namespace's same-simple-name constructor, a root-level creation cannot guess a namespace, and a compiler-rejected semantic-project constructor remains unrelated
cases.assertions: balanced generic normalization preserves the nested constructor identity, parentheses preserve exact inline-New receiver provenance, lexical namespace evidence selects only its own constructor, root-level unqualified names cannot bridge into an unrelated namespace, and compiler-rejected semantic fallback cannot be rescued by another projectless root

cases.shape: one projectless Web Forms source index contains a dropdown Init handler and a data-access constructor that populates a list by calling through service, repository, and SQL gateway methods; an uncalled same-name method in the constructor's class is an implicit-Me decoy
cases.assertions: bounded single-index graph admission retains the constructor declaration and body facts instead of silently losing the side-effect terminal, while inline-New receiver evidence never bridges to the same-name implicit-Me decoy

cases.shape: a Web Forms handler calls two same-named Run methods in separate classes within one source file; both continue two levels and converge on one SQL terminal
cases.assertions: the packet retains two bounded event-chain routes while the complete supported-terminal inventory counts their shared terminal once

cases.shape: syntax receiver closure exceeds the deliberately tiny traversal-work budget before graph composition
cases.assertions: the packet reports graph-syntax-closure-work as an input limit and never classifies the page-three analogue as a complete zero-terminal result
